title: Micro-Repair
concept: The smallest way to make up, for when a sharp word has stung: one of you softens your tone and owns the impact in a sentence, before it hardens into something bigger. A clumsy repair today beats a perfect one next week.
whenToUse: When a remark came out sharp or something small stung, and a full repair feels like too much but leaving it will make it worse. Start within minutes if you can; finish within 24 hours.
steps: Do one small thing: make one kind move, or own your part out loud.
Sit side by side instead of face to face if that’s easier.
Say you noticed the impact, in one sentence, with no “but”.
Take one tiny next step, or a Pause + Return if you need one.

phrases.text: That came out sharp. Let me try again.
I saw that hurt you. I’m sorry for ___.

working: B is short about the bins. Thirty seconds later B says, “That came out sharp.” They sit side by side on the sofa and B owns the tone. By bedtime they’re talking about tomorrow.
notWorking: A bites back on Monday, then saves the repair for “the real talk this weekend”. By Friday nobody remembers the first sharp word, only that every evening has felt tense.
activity: Pick one small, low-stakes thing from today. Soften your tone, own your part, and make one small ask. Aim to start within minutes.
